q: I've read that babies are loud sleepers but had no idea how loud they are. My boy is a spitter so all the grunting, squeaking, wheezing and other weird noises he's making are keeping me up at night.
cx: First-time mother of an almost three-week-old.

q: My husband believes all is fine and will be good so no need to worry or, for that matter, we shouldn't even think about unpleasant/ potentially unsafe things.
cx: Husband's response to her night-time fears about the baby.

q:
I wake up with back pain no matter how I sleep - and I can’t sleep on my back or belly anymore. I bump into everything.

I’m tired!!
cx: 31 weeks and done with being pregnant.

q:
So far I've tried:

* Pregnancy pillow/pillows between my legs
* Mattress topper
* Hot water bottle
* Ice packs
* Warm baths before bed
* Massage
* Spiky massage ball
* Various stretches/exercises
* Pregnancy Yoga […] * Physio
* Osteopathy
cx: Months of one-sided hip pain at night in late pregnancy.

q:
Physio gave me a little relief for a couple of days after each session but never stopped the pain completely. My first osteopathy appointment made a really noticeable difference for about a week, but unfortunately the second appointment hasn't had the same effect and the pain is back to how it was originally.

I'm desperate for some sleep and wondering if there's anything else I haven't thought of.
cx: How the paid treatments landed.

q: He typically works 3:30 pm - 12 am but occasionally a later shift or overtime. This leaves me in the evenings to get home from work & take care of 2 little ones while my back hurts & im tired from pregnancy.
cx: Pregnant with a third; husband works nights.

q: As soon as my husband gets home, he will try helping with the 1.5 year old if she wakes up. Most of the time it’s on me. And lately he’s been getting off at 2 am so he’s on a different schedule than us. On saturdays, he’s so tired that he wakes up around 10 am and me and the kids have been up since 6 am. He will wake up and tell me to take a nap so he can tap in
cx: How the week's nights and Saturday mornings are split.

q: I probably wake up 3-8 times a night, I usually can’t sleep when everyone else goes to sleep because I either have to clean, do school work, shower, and once in a while do something I enjoy (sewing, painting, or just watch tv).
cx: Two children, full-time college student, partner works long hours.
r: mental health (post centred on chronic depression and anxiety)

q: i told him my girls pediatrician said its important i get ATLEAST 4 hours of uninterrupted sleep so i dont fall into a bad headspace, atleast a few times a week.
cx: Two weeks after a c-section, with older twins at home.

q: yet when i told him it was his turn to feed our daughter tonight he said “you got it” and when i asked if he would be on baby duty tonight so i could get good rest he had literally no comment, heard the baby crying and watched me get up to make a bottle for her and then rolled over and went to sleep.
cx: She had asked for one night a week off; this was the first.

q: I feel disappointed, upset, hurt, and sad because i wanted more support. I want my husband to love me enough to be able to sacrifice some sleep for me
cx: After he rolled over on his night.

q: i have help during the weekdays since im not supposed to lift my twins after my c section and that’s why i dont press my husband to get up with the baby at night since he works long hours driving and the person helping out lets me get some extra sleep in the morning but i still have my newborn at all times.
cx: Why she rarely asks him for nights.

q: I’ve tried the pillow between the legs and even one on top of my head for comfort but even now at 18w I can’t sleep until I’m super tired at like 1am and usually always wake up at 7am and it’s not even continuous sleep because I toss and turn trying to find a comfortable spot.
cx: Sleep got harder from week 15.

q: My husband gets on my nerves even though we’re both small people in KING SIZE BED because it’s like I need the ENTIRE bed and ALL the pillows.
cx: Sharing the bed at 18 weeks.

q: I don’t have a pregnancy pillow yet since there’s soooo many different ones that idek which one would work or if it’s actually worth it.
cx: Weighing a pregnancy pillow.

q:
I usually try not to take any meds except tylenol if i’m absolutely miserable with a headache or body aches but it doesn’t help my heartburn.

Please help I am exhausted
cx: Heartburn keeps her awake.

q: Last night, we started using a new Cradlewise crib and I was so pissed that he woke up at night again.
cx: Sixteen-month-old with four split nights in a row.

q: My husband heard and stepped in so I could sleep but it scared me that I got so mad so fast. I’m desperate to sleep more than two hours in a row.
cx: After losing her temper at a toddler awake at night.

q: We were up from 12-3 last night and he was awake at 6:45 this morning.
cx: The night before she posted.

q: He would do nights with me, but not in a helpful way. He would just stay up with me whenever I fed her until one night he picked her up in her sleep and totally freaked me out. I told him he had to stop, that him sitting up with me and become sleep deprived is not helpful.
cx: How her husband handled nights on paternity leave.

q: I’ve made the decision to stop pumping &doing night feeds when my baby is only 3 months and I can’t stop crying. I just can’t physically do it anymore and with the sleep deprivation everything is taking a toll on me.  I don’t know why I’m so emotional over it and I feel so guilty because I made it to 10 months with my first baby :(
cx: Second baby; ending pumping because of the nights.

q: It’s getting to the point though where it’s really taking a toll on my back walking and rocking him for every nap/bedtime. He’s almost 18 pounds. I also lose my nights entirely because since he’s in bed between 7-7:30, that means I am too. And I miss my husband.
cx: Parents take shifts with a nearly six-month-old; considering Ferber.

q:
The insomnia is making me lose it. 

I’ve been trying the unisom and b6, and while it lets me maybe get a few hours of sleep it isn’t doing anything for the nausea and vomitting.
cx: Seven weeks pregnant with a 13-month-old at home.

q: To make it all worse I have a 13 month old and am a SAHM and I feel so guilty I barely have anything left in me to give him. Just standing up is a chore.
cx: Insomnia and nausea in early pregnancy with a baby at home.

q: But I’m only able to actually sleep if it’s my husband with the baby. Anyone else, like my mom or dad, for example, I can’t genuinely sleep. My best friend lives about 40 minutes away and has a baby the same age and has offered to take off work to come watch him so I can sleep some, but I don’t think it’ll work bc I don’t think I’ll actually be able to sleep.
cx: Husband away on the road most of the month; parents nearby.
r: mental health (post centred on rage; mentions insomnia)

q: I’m exhausted. I just want to sleep and do nothing. (Not looking for sleep advice — my husband and I take sleep very seriously but we have a FOMO baby who sleeps great during the day but likes to wake up every 2-3 hours at night. Sometimes she nurses back to sleep, sometimes she likes to party for two hours)
cx: Mother of a 13-month-old.

q: We have no village, it’s just the two of us since day 1. We are business owners, we work during her naps and take shifts watching our daughter during the day so the other one can work.
cx: How the couple divides days.

q:
My husband is the best ever, we are in it together 50/50, and I couldn’t ask for anyone better. So why am I so angry and tired? 

I know some women have it harder than me and I feel like I don’t have the right to be upset but I just am.
cx: An equal split and still exhausted.
